---
title: "Offline-first and online data"
---

## Offline-first rule

A capability that can reasonably work offline should do so. Online dependencies must be explicit rather than accidental. Cached/shared resources should be managed at the app/service layer where they benefit more than one capability.

## Online APIs

The current source includes a generic `api.get` capability and module-owned API definitions/consumers in specialist modules. Online providers must document provider, terms/licence, attribution, credentials, privacy implications and what leaves the device.

The Master Book identifies important service areas including Open-Meteo, GDACS, World Bank indicators, exchange-rate providers, map/tile providers and RFC 3161 timestamp authorities.

## Location privacy

Location-aware API calls should minimise disclosure. Prefer sending only the precision actually required for the task and make online use visible to the user where relevant.

## Credentials

Secrets belong in appropriate shared/settings storage and should not be baked into preset exports, logs, documentation examples or return payloads.

## RSS / Atom

Feed consumption belongs in the same online-data model: explicit provider, bounded network behaviour, cache/offline behaviour and no silent cross-capability special cases.
